title: The rule of 16: the market's implied one-day move
summary: To get the market's implied one-day move, divide implied volatility by 16. A $100 stock with 32% IV has a one-day move of about 2%, so about two-thirds of the time it trades between $98 and $102. The 16 comes from the square root of 252 trading days, which is 15.87.

params.label: Excess drift over rate
params.help: Your view of annual return above the risk-free rate. Zero = the market view; EV is then about zero.

steps.caption: One standard deviation: 32 / 16 = 2%, so $98 to $102 about two-thirds of the time.
Two standard deviations, about $96 to $104, cover about 95% under the model.
Why 16: one day is 1/252 of a year, and the square root of 252 is 15.87.

takeaways: One-day implied move is roughly IV divided by 16.
32% IV on a $100 stock gives about a $2 (2%) daily move.
16 is the square root of 252 trading days, rounded.
caveats: Real returns have fat tails; moves beyond the bands happen more often than the normal model says.
The chart uses calendar days for dte, so the band differs slightly from the 252-day rule.
